name: Jehoiakim
overview: Jehoiakim, also known as Eliakim, was made king of Judah by Pharaoh Nechoh following the death of his father Josiah. Beginning his reign at age twenty-five, he ruled for eleven years and is noted for doing evil in the sight of the Lord, continuing the sinful patterns of his predecessors. During his reign, Jehoiakim became a servant to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, for three years before rebelling, which led to divine judgment through invasions by surrounding nations as foretold by the prophets. His reign ended in wickedness and overthrow, and he was succeeded by his son Jehoiachin; notably, Jehoiakim is also listed as an ancestor of Jesus, linking his legacy to the Messiah.
